drhp.business: IVP Limited, founded in 1929 and now part of the Allana Group, manufactures foundry chemicals (no-bake and shell resins, coatings and allied consumables), polyurethane foam systems for footwear, and PU laminating adhesives for flexible packaging, alongside composites, insulation and refractory/powder resins. It produces from two plants at Tarapur (Maharashtra) and Bengaluru and serves more than 500 customers in India and overseas markets across the foundry, footwear, composites, insulation and packaging industries. risks.note: Listed by management under Threats. IVP's inputs are crude-linked chemical feedstocks: the MD&A notes that geopolitical tensions, particularly in West Asia, have introduced volatility into global energy markets and affected crude oil and feedstock prices, creating intermittent pressure on input costs, logistics and inflation expectations. Management states that volatility in raw material and energy costs affects profitability and limits pricing flexibility, and cites raw material volatility and supply chain disruption as near-term challenges in the footwear PU segment.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and supply disruption

risks.note: Flagged under Concerns as 'continued margin pressure in commodity markets'. In foundry chemicals, commoditisation in standard products continues to pressure margins and rising competition from low-cost players intensifies pricing pressure. The footwear PU market is fragmented and MSME-dominated with high price sensitivity and cost-driven decision-making. IVP's stated response is to move up the value chain and expand into value-added products, so margin outcomes depend on executing that mix shift.

The foundry industry is cyclically dependent on the automotive, infrastructure and engineering sectors, with a significant share of customers being MSMEs that are more vulnerable to demand and cost fluctuations. Management describes demand trends as uneven. IVP's diversification into footwear PU and packaging adhesives is explicitly positioned as the mitigant for this single-segment cyclicality.
risks.risk: Cyclical end-market dependence in foundry chemicals

risks.note: Named under Threats. Competition is described as most intense in commoditised foundry products, where low-cost players pressure pricing, and IVP's defence rests on technical service, application expertise and customer-specific formulation rather than price.
risks.risk: Intensifying competition from domestic and international players

risks.note: Named under Risks. Increasingly stringent environmental regulation is driving the need for higher investment in sustainable and compliant technologies across the foundry chemicals industry, and the flexible packaging adhesives business carries product-safety and food-contact regulatory requirements in critical applications. IVP operates chemical plants under an ISO 9001/14001/45001 Integrated Management System and states it remains fully compliant with applicable safety and environmental regulations.
risks.risk: Regulatory risk relating to environmental and safety compliance

risks.note: Named under Risks. Production is concentrated in just two sites — Tarapur (the primary hub for foundry binders, coatings and polyurethane) and Bengaluru (foundry coatings) — so an interruption at Tarapur in particular would affect most of the portfolio.
